briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Worsening Climate Crisis Warnings and the Urgency of Adaptation
sections.content: Recently, the chilling phrase 'historic first' has frequently appeared in relation to the climate crisis, emphasizing the severity of the situation [4]. In particular, a 'Godzilla-grade' super El Niño is currently heating the planet and could be the strongest in at least a thousand years, while climate change is influencing extreme weather phenomena such as Nor'easters [26, 33, 52]. Such climate change is exacerbating the threat of extreme heat to human health and severely impacting child nutrition [24, 39]. Furthermore, research has been published indicating that three glaciers in British Columbia (B.C.) face extinction within decades [45, 46]. Amidst the outgoing UN Secretary-General issuing a grave warning about climate change [34], an analysis suggests that corporate survival depends on 'substantive adaptation' beyond mere metrics [2], and major international organizations are strengthening global response efforts by establishing a joint framework for 'climate adaptation' [3].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Practices and Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: Various efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals are expanding both domestically and internationally. Yongin City is providing up to 100,000 KRW based on reduction performance through its vehicle carbon neutrality point system [5], while Pohang City, Gwangmyeong City, and the Inje Rotary Club are encouraging carbon neutrality practices in daily life through campaigns like 'World Car-Free Day' and recruitment for 'Net-Zero Energy Cafes' [6, 7, 9]. Internationally, a non-profit organization in Baltimore is addressing climate change by providing trees and jobs to underserved communities [37], and in the UK, the cost of driving electric vehicles has become up to nine times cheaper than gasoline or diesel cars, accelerating the transition to eco-friendly mobility [54]. In the renewable energy sector, the share of renewables in Australia's main electricity market reached a record high of 80.5% [10], and domestic local governments continue their efforts, with Chuncheon City being selected for the renewable energy convergence support project for the ninth consecutive year [11]. KEPCO KPS made its first overseas renewable energy investment by acquiring a stake in an Indonesian hydropower plant [12], and investment attraction is also active, with renewable energy company AMPIN raising $100 million from a Norwegian fund [16]. These positive domestic and international advancements are occurring as the 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Report investigates the drivers and constraints of global carbon neutrality [8].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Policy Tasks in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Globally, the pressure to accelerate renewable energy transition is increasing, but a significant gap still exists in achieving targets. According to the Irena report, renewable energy capacity reached 5.15 TW in 2025, falling short of the target of 11.2 TW [14]. In particular, the pressure to 'double' renewable energy to achieve 2030 climate targets presents both an opportunity and a challenge for Korean industries and exports [13]. Domestically, a public hearing is scheduled for the reorganization of the renewable energy contract market [15], and in the Jeju region, a 'grid contribution' evaluation has been introduced for solar and wind power generation facilities, leading to complex power grid connection issues where settlement amounts differ even for the same power source [17]. Furthermore, the acceleration of 'green transition' in overseas fashion supply chains is expected to significantly impact the fate of Korea's textile and apparel industries [18]. This situation highlights policy challenges, including comments suggesting the need for fundamental legal and policy changes beyond market-based approaches to climate change [22], and cases like the climate change superfund law being blocked in New York [35].

sections.title: 🌍 Strengthening International Cooperation and the Dual Nature of AI Technology
sections.content: World leaders are urging action on climate change at the UN General Assembly, emphasizing the importance of international solidarity [32, 44]. During the UN General Assembly's foreign ministers' dialogue, climate change and ecosystem degradation were discussed as national security risks, indicating a growing awareness of the severity of the issue [48, 50]. China's climate action plans are taking concrete shape, with nearly three-quarters of the 72 five-year plans announced this year including climate change and energy-related policies or targets [53]. Meanwhile, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a crucial tool in responding to climate change. The Korea Rural Community Corporation is discussing AI-based water management in cooperation with Taiwan [1], and Germany is redesigning its power grid for the renewable energy era using AI [19]. However, various perspectives exist regarding AI's role and impact, including an editorial stating that AI has joined the race against climate change [42], and reports that Jensen Huang spoke 'like a supervillain' about AI and climate change [20]. There is also an analysis suggesting that economic agendas are driving the climate change debate [43].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing reaffirmed the severity of the climate crisis, while also highlighting various domestic and international efforts to overcome it, as well as the role of new technologies and policy challenges. We must continue to enhance climate resilience through ongoing attention and cooperation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
